tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when the user asks to review, audit, assess, or health-check...'), focuses on user intent and operational problems (timeouts, throttling, cold starts, etc.) rather than internal implementation, and explicitly lists many trigger phrases and contexts ('serverless review', 'Lambda operational review', etc.). It is a dense but single, well-structured paragraph that stays within a reasonable length for the breadth of scope covered.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user asks to review, audit, assess, or health-check serverless functions or applications, or raises Lambda timeouts, throttling, concurrency limits, cold starts, memory sizing, missing dead-letter queues... Triggers on requests like 'serverless review', 'Lambda operational review', 'review my Lambda functions'..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into domain-specific procedures (API calls, derived metric formulas, severity rules) without explaining general concepts like what Lambda or DynamoDB are. It assumes AWS/serverless familiarity and focuses on project-specific conventions.
tests.evidence: Make **one** `cloudwatch.GetMetricData` call per resource. `Period: 21600` (6 hours). `StartTime`: 7 days ago.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Tables in the body (budget caps, alarm metric summary, cost opportunities) are concise summaries, not exhaustive reference data — the detailed catalogs (check ids, thresholds, full metric lists) are explicitly pushed to references/ files like checks-lambda.md and metrics-and-logs.md.
tests.evidence: `references/metrics-and-logs.md` lists the exact metric set per resource type ... Use it rather than improvising a metric list

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ has at least one markdown link in the body.
tests.evidence: [references/collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md), [references/checks-event-sources.md](references/checks-event-sources.md), etc. are all linked, e.g. 'use `references/collection-reference.md`' is prose but markdown links like `references/report-template.md` appear via `Use the structure in `references/report-template.md`.`

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.message: Verdict not allowed for this test: 'warning' (allowed: passed, failed, skipped)

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (SQS visibility timeout vs function timeout check, severity assignment, secret redaction) are prescriptive, while flexible steps (collection order in Steps 4-8, selection of findings) explicitly allow freedom with rationale.
tests.evidence: Steps 4 through 8 are independent of each other once Step 3 is done, so collect them in whatever order is convenient

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple tools/options could apply (e.g., Lambda Power Tuning for memory, CLI/SAM/CDK remediation snippets), the skill designates a clear default or primary approach rather than listing equal alternatives.
tests.evidence: Always state that memory changes should be validated with [AWS Lambda Power Tuning](https://github.com/alexcasalboni/aws-lambda-power-tuning) rather than applied blind

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable 10-step review procedure applicable to any serverless workload scope, not a one-off instance; specifics like templates and check catalogs are embedded within this reusable approach.
tests.evidence: Ask the user what to review. Accept any of: ... An application or stack boundary ... All resources of a family in named Regions

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Known API Quirks' section with concrete, specific corrections to non-obvious AWS API behaviors.
tests.evidence: `lambda.GetFunctionConcurrency` returning empty means the function is **unreserved**, not that its concurrency is zero.
